_provenance.note: Mississippi citation authorities. Mississippi's operative SNAP policy lives in the SNAP Policy Manual (Title 18, Part 14 of the Mississippi Administrative Code), cited internally as bare 'Rule ##.#' (e.g. 'Rule 15.1', 'Rule 22.14', 'Rule 13.12'). This pack writes 'MS Rule' before a citation in running prose purely for cross-state disambiguation (matching this roster's general convention), while the regex below matches the bare 'Rule ##.##' form Mississippi's own manual uses natively. This pack ALSO cites two real Mississippi Code Annotated sections (§43-12-71, the drug-felony opt-out; §43-12-19, the ABAWD waiver-authority statute), so this pack defines a SECOND citation family, 'mscode', matching this roster's Connecticut, Kentucky, Alabama, and Louisiana packs' multi-family pattern.

patterns.note: Mississippi SNAP Policy Manual (Title 18, Part 14), bare 'Rule ##.##' numbering, e.g. Rule 15.1 (Categorically Eligible Households - General), Rule 22.14 (Individuals Convicted of Drug-Related Felonies), Rule 13.12 (ABAWD Waivers).

Mississippi Code Annotated, Title 43 (Public Welfare), Chapter 12 (Food Stamps/SNAP-related provisions), cited by section number. This pack cites two: §43-12-71 (drug-related felony SNAP eligibility, opt-out effective July 1, 2019) and §43-12-19 (ABAWD waiver authority requiring a natural-disaster declaration and Governor's approval).

msrule.note: Application Process - three steps: filing, interview, verification
Expedited Service - Screening Requirements: <$150 gross income and <=$100 liquid resources; destitute migrant/seasonal farmworkers; or combined income+resources less than rent/mortgage+utilities
Exemptions to General Work Requirements - age 60+ or under 16 exempt (distinct from the ABAWD 18-64 age band in Rule 13.1)
ABAWD General Rule - age 18 but under 65, under-14 dependent exemption, 3 countable months per 36-month period; revised May 2026 (current OBBBA-era parameters)

ABAWD Waivers - MDHS may seek a waiver only during a formal state or federal natural-disaster declaration with the Governor's approval; cites Miss. Code Ann. §43-12-19 - a Mississippi-specific statutory gate distinct from the federal unemployment-rate waiver criteria most other states use

Categorically Eligible Households - General: categorical eligibility limited strictly to households where every member receives or is eligible for TANF and/or SSI - Mississippi has NO income-based BBCE track
Categorically Eligible Households - Income and Resource Exceptions: categorically eligible households are exempt from gross income, net income, AND resource maximums entirely

Resources - General: MDHS applies 'uniform national resource standards of eligibility ... published every October 1st by USDA' - no Mississippi-specific dollar figure published in the manual itself; also states MDHS exempts most vehicles to align with MS TANF policy
Excluded Resources - subsection H excludes MOST vehicles used for regular transportation entirely, with no fair-market-value threshold
Value of Non-Excluded Recreational Vehicles - counted only above $4,650 excess fair market value or equity value, whichever is higher
Standard Deduction - 8.31% of the monthly net income eligibility standard for household sizes 1-6, national minimum-standard formula per 7 CFR 273.9(d)(1)(i)
Excess Medical Deduction - actual verified expenses over $35/month for an elderly or disabled household member; no flat Standard Medical Deduction shortcut
Excess Shelter Deduction - capped at the FNS national maximum unless the household contains an elderly or disabled member (then uncapped)
Standard Utility Allowances - SUA (heating/cooling), BUA (2+ other utilities), and standard telephone allowance; structure only, no MS-specific dollar figures published in the manual
Individuals Convicted of Drug-Related Felonies - Mississippi fully opted out of the federal drug-felony SNAP ban effective July 1, 2019; cites Miss. Code Ann. §43-12-71
ESAP Eligibility - ALL household members must be age 65 or older (not 60) with no earned income; mandatory track, ineligible for regular SNAP if qualified
Certification periods may be lengthened up to 24 months for all-elderly/disabled households, 12 months for other households

mscode.note: Eligibility for TANF or SNAP benefits following certain criminal convictions - Mississippi's full opt-out of the federal drug-related-felony SNAP ban, effective July 1, 2019 (formerly HB 1352, 2019 regular session)
ABAWD waiver authority - MDHS may seek a waiver of ABAWD time limits only during a formal state or federal declaration of a natural disaster, with the Governor's approval
